newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end week just below all-time high.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end week just below all-time high.

text.p: French shares closed at a fresh record close on Friday, just below an all-time trading high, as the market continued its bull run started on January 2 -- fuelled by new investor cash and a firmer dollar.
Special factors such as big rises in blue chips LVMH and Canal Plus also underpinned the index.
The blue-chip CAC-40 index closed up 17.33 points or 0.72 percent at 2,425.10 and set an all time high at 2,426.13.
The index gained 4.2 percent this week.
The CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,429 from 2,408 on Thursday's close.
Total volume was 9.97 billion francs, including foreign shares, among which 6.56 billion francs in blue-chip shares.
"The market is fundamentally bullish. There is an enormous wave of buying," a trader said, noting a lot of basket deals by funds that follow the CAC-40 index.

"The market wants to rise. New York is busy breaking new records and so are we," another trader said. "There is a lot of volume, loads of cash is being invested and that is going to continue," he said.
But the higher the market gets the more some players are getting nervous about a possible downward correction.
This uncertainty fuels a string of market rumours which carry hopes corporate deals could further boost price levels.
"There is a restless search for new ideas to keep rising and the moment there is something to chew on the market goes for it," a trader said.

Havas on Thursday evening announced it was going to buy out minorities in its 74 percent unit CEP Communication for 407 francs per share, or 2.7 billion francs. Havas shares closed 0.20 percent lower at 400 on the news but had made gains for two days on the rumour.

Another big deal which started with a whisper in the morning and quickly echoed round the markets before confirmation was the sale by luxury goods group LVMH of a seven percent stake in Britain's Guinness Plc, reducing its stake to 14 percent.
LVMH was rewarded for the move with a 3.26 percent rise to 1,551 francs and earlier set a historic high at 1,584 francs.

Canal Plus managed to dispell some doubts about its digital pay television unit in France by saying that the division, Canalsatellite, had 220,000 subscribers. The share closed 6.67 percent higher at 1,216 francs.
